key_idea: Colour the triangulation's vertices with 3 colours so every triangle has one vertex of each colour, then guard with the smallest colour class.
reason: The 3-colouring turns a geometric covering problem into a counting argument where pigeonhole gives ⌊n/3⌋ at once, and the bound then feels inevitable. It is short, has no cases, and uses only the existence of a triangulation and ears, so it is a classic book proof.
recognized: Fisk's proof of Chvátal's Art Gallery Theorem (Proofs from THE BOOK)
